fieldNotes.location: Confirmed UNFI Montgomery NY DC (Hudson Valley DC), 525 Neelytown Rd, Montgomery NY 12549. Roster ROOFTOP geocode 41.493552,-74.235922 lands squarely on a large L-shaped distribution building off Neelytown Rd in the Orange County / Hudson Valley region. Web-corroborated: UNFI press release - Hudson Valley DC opened 2014, LEED Gold, built to serve the NYC-metro Whole Foods customer base.
fieldNotes.buildingShape: Large L-shaped DC building. Continuous dock-door rhythm along the W and NW long faces with ~75 trailers backed in and parked across the imagery. A small separate ancillary building sits SE of the main DC (likely a fleet/maintenance shop) -> buildingCount 2; multipleFacilities left false because the second building is small and ancillary, not a co-equal large cluster (flagged).
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Continuous bands of dock doors on the W and NW faces; ~75 trailers backed/parked -> band 50+ (estimated ~90 positions).
fieldNotes.dropYard: A large marked trailer-parking lot occupies the NW corner of the property holding many trailers without tractors -> dropYard true, dropArea band 50+.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Single private access road serves the property from Neelytown Rd; the truck drive wraps the W side of the building into the dock aprons and NW drop yard. Street View on Neelytown Rd (2025-03) shows the building set well back behind employee parking; the truck gate is not directly resolved in the road-level imagery. A controlled gate with a staffed booth is assumed for a modern (2014) LEED Gold UNFI DC serving NYC-metro Whole Foods -> truckGate true, guardShack true, remoteGs false; all flagged medium-confidence.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Docks concentrated on the W/NW faces of the L-shaped building as one continuous dock system, not two clearly separated ship/rcv banks on opposing faces -> false.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Long approach from Neelytown Rd through the property to the deep dock aprons -> drivewayLong true.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Wide access road and large open paved apron -> physical room for an express/bypass lane.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: The Town of Montgomery, Orange County NY is a small Hudson Valley community; the parcel is bordered by woods and open land with scattered rural/industrial development -> per rubric, Rural.
fieldNotes.railServed: No rail spur enters the property; truck-served grocery DC.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: ~48 acres derived from the perimeter box around the building, dock aprons, drop yard, and employee parking.
fieldNotes.entryLanes/exitLanes: Estimated 2/2; gate not directly resolved in Street View.

citations.claim: UNFI's FY2025 Form 10-K, Item 2 Properties, lists a distribution centre at "Montgomery, New York" as of 2025-08-02. Our roster address for this record is "525 Neelytown Rd, Montgomery, NY 12549".

divestitureCheck.method: Checked against UNFI's FY2025 10-K property table and against its publicly announced 2025-2026 network consolidation. UNFI has closed 12 distribution centres in six years, so presence on the 10-K list alone is not treated as proof of current operation; the announced closures were checked by name.
divestitureCheck.result: present on the FY2025 property list and not named in any announced closure

sources.covers: UNFI network optimisation, the Allentown PA closure, and Central-region consolidations

verification.claimScope: CITY-LEVEL identity only. The 10-K names the city, not the parcel. This record is `probable` rather than `confirmed` because no retrieved source ties UNFI to the specific parcel traced here.
verification.rationale: PROBABLE: UNFI's own SEC 10-K property table lists a distribution centre in Montgomery, New York as of 2025-08-02, and this record sits in that city. That establishes the company operates a DC there. It does NOT establish that the parcel traced here is that DC, and no source retrieved in this pass closes that gap, so the verdict stops at probable.
